# Known finding-set diffs between guff and golangci-lint (R21).
# Format: <target> <guff-only|golangci-only> <normalized-key>
# normalized-key = relpath:line:linter:message
# Regenerated by: ./compat/run.sh --update-allowlist
#
# Prefer fixing guff over growing this list. Entries here are accepted
# mismatches (message phrasing, enable-set gaps, known DEFERRED).
#
# WARNING: `--update-allowlist` rewrites this file from the current diff and
# drops the comments below. The rationale is kept in
# docs/COMPAT-HARDENING.md §4 (2026-09-06 続き 209), which is the copy to read
# and to update.
#
# Keys are pinned to tailscale v1.102.3 (corpus/hunt.json), so the line numbers
# are stable until that ref moves.
#
# revive `time-equal` ×4 — guff is right and golangci-lint 2.12.2 cannot
# report this rule at all.
#
# `rule/time_equal.go` opens with a guard no other revive rule has:
#
#     w := &lintTimeEqual{file, onFailure}
#     if w.file.Pkg.TypeCheck() != nil {
#         return nil
#     }
#
# golangci-lint hands revive only a list of *file names*
# (`pkg/golinters/revive/revive.go`: `revive.Lint([][]string{GetGoFileNames(pass)}, …)`),
# so revive type-checks the package itself with `importer.Default()`. That
# check returns an error inside golangci-lint's process, and this rule — alone
# among revive's 102 — throws its whole file away when it does.
#
# Measured against golangci-lint 2.12.2 / revive v1.15.0 on 2026-09-06:
#
#   * revive's own `testdata/time_equal.go`, whose four comparisons are
#     annotated `// MATCH /use t.Equal(u) instead of "==" operator/`, produces
#     **zero** findings under golangci-lint. guff reports exactly those four.
#   * The rule is enabled and reaches revive: `GL_DEBUG=revive` prints
#     "Enabled by config rules (1): time-equal", and `exported` reports in the
#     same run.
#   * Type information is *not* the missing piece. In one file, one run,
#     `string-of-int` — type-info-dependent but unguarded — fires while
#     `time-equal` stays silent. `Package.TypeCheck` keeps its partial
#     `types.Info` even when the check errors ("Remember the typechecking info,
#     even if config.Check failed"), so every other rule still sees types.
#
# So the divergence is upstream's integration, not guff's port, and the four
# findings here are true positives: three `time.Time` `!=`/`==` comparisons in
# tests and one in `net/dns/resolver/tsdns.go:704`. They stay reported.
#
# Delete these four lines when golangci-lint's revive wrapper starts supplying
# type information (or revive drops the guard) — at that point upstream reports
# them too and the diff closes on its own.

tailscale guff-only cmd/natc/ippool/consensusippool_test.go:184:revive:time-equal: use !ww.LastUsed.Equal(time1) instead of "!=" operator
tailscale guff-only cmd/natc/ippool/consensusippool_test.go:201:revive:time-equal: use !ww.LastUsed.Equal(time2) instead of "!=" operator
tailscale guff-only net/dns/resolver/tsdns.go:704:revive:time-equal: use c.mod.Equal(cur.mod) instead of "==" operator
tailscale guff-only wgengine/magicsock/magicsock_test.go:3490:revive:time-equal: use newTime.Equal(lastRebindTime) instead of "==" operator
